sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Read the descriptions. (i) A filling stitch where the thread is visible only on the face of the fabric, creating floats only on the front side. (ii) A stitch worked between two lines with interlocking diagonal threads, often used for thick seams or connecting areas. Identify the stitches. Options: (a) Darning stitch (b) Herringbone stitch (c) Blanket stitch (d) Long and short stitch.

Rahul is embroidering a garment. Part A: Which of the following is not part of darning stitch? (i) It is a filling stitch (ii) The stitch is visible only on the face of the fabric (iii) The front has floats (iv) The thread floats cross in the middle forming an X. Part B: Which stitch should he use for finishing edges in a patchwork?
questions.answer: Part A: (iv), because that describes cross stitch. Part B: buttonhole stitch.

questions.q: State True or False. (a) A knot may be used to start the embroidery. (b) The back of the embroidery should be as neat as the front.
questions.answer: (a) False: start with a back stitch. (b) True.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Satin stitch (b) Stem stitch. B: (i) Outline stitch (ii) Smooth filling stitch (iii) Loops on the surface.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why is it recommended to avoid using a knot at the start of embroidery work? What is the correct way to begin instead?
questions.answer: A knot makes a lump and shows on the front and can come undone. Begin with a back stitch, which is strong and neat.

questions.q: What is the difference between buttonhole stitch and blanket stitch?
questions.answer: Both are looped edge stitches. In buttonhole stitch the stitches are very close together; in blanket stitch they are a little distance apart.

questions.q: Name any two filling stitches.
questions.answer: Satin stitch and long and short stitch (also darning stitch).

questions.q: Where is chain stitch used?
questions.answer: It is used for heavy outlines, or in rows following the outline as a filling.

questions.q: State two points about the finishing of an embroidered article.
questions.answer: Clip the extra threads at the back and wash or dry clean the article. Starch and iron it well and finish the edges by hemming or picoting.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the steps of making a satin stitch and a French knot stitch.
questions.answer: (i) Satin stitch: work straight stitches slantwise, taking the thread out equally at the front and back so that the surface is smooth, e.g. from top to bottom for straight areas. (ii) French knot: bring the thread up through the fabric and wrap it over and under the needle. (iii) Then insert the needle into the fabric close to where it came up; use double thread for a larger knot.

questions.q: Uma is embroidering a baby blanket with multicoloured butterflies. Suggest two stitches to fill the motif and one for the edge, with reasons.
questions.answer: (i) Satin stitch gives a smooth filling for wings. (ii) Long and short stitch fills shaded colours. (iii) Blanket stitch for the edge because it is the traditional finish for blankets.

questions.q: Explain the steps of back stitch (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Thread the needle and insert it where the embroidery begins. (ii) Pick a few threads of the fabric and pull the needle and thread through. (iii) Repeat at the same place picking a few extra threads; it is worked on the wrong side from right to left.

questions.q: Explain how the finishing of an embroidered article is done (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Do not end in a big knot; keep the back neat and clip extra threads. (ii) Wash or dry clean, starch and iron it. (iii) Finish the edges by hemming or picoting and store in mulmul cloth.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the ten basic embroidery stitches briefly.
questions.answer: (i) Stem stitch is an outline stitch and satin stitch a smooth filling. (ii) Long and short stitch fills shaded areas and chain stitch makes loops for outlines. (iii) Darning stitch has floats only on the face. (iv) Herringbone stitch is worked between two lines. (v) Buttonhole stitch has close stitches and blanket stitch has spaced stitches for edges. (vi) Cross stitch forms X's and French knot is a wrapped knot.
